headline: Benchmarks for AI virtual cell models are being tested for scientific validity
label: Rigorous Evaluation Of Biological Models
summary: Perturbation-prediction benchmarks for AI virtual cell models are under scrutiny as new work asks whether they measure scientific value and whether discoveries…
synthesis: The dominant thread is whether predictive models in biology are assessed in ways that reflect scientific value rather than predictive accuracy alone. A preprint argues that current perturbation-prediction benchmarks for AI virtual cell models fail to measure scientific value and introduces PerturbHD as an evaluation framework. TxConformal addresses a related concern from a statistical angle, using conformal selection with representation balancing to control false discoveries under distribution shift in AI-driven therapeutic discovery. HyperMap and scPert advance perturbation-response prediction through meta-learning and multimodal LLM-knowledge fusion, respectively, and do not center on evaluation. The remaining items, a mouse strain prioritization resource, a pH-sensitive protein scoring framework, and an R Shiny multi-omics browser, are tool or resource papers outside this focus. What is new is explicit attention to whether benchmarks and selection procedures support valid scientific conclusions.
